tweets.text: On July 27, 1953, the guns fell silent on the Korean Peninsula after three years of brutal fighting. The Korean War is often called the Forgotten War, but the men who fought will always be remembered for their courage and sacrifice. They held the line in bitter cold and impossible terrain, often outnumbered, often overlooked back home. Their service secured freedom for millions of South Koreans who still live in it today. On this National Korean War Veterans Armistice Day, we honor all who served, especially the more than 36,000 Americans who never came home. We remember the Chosin Few and tell the story of those who fought so no generation forgets the men of the Forgotten War.
